title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation and Memory Management
description: Paper introducing MUSE-Autoskill, a framework for self-evolving AI agents that can create, manage, and evaluate their own skills. The system enables agents to continuously improve through skill creation, memory management, and evaluation mechanisms. Demonstrates advances in agentic AI capabilities for autonomous skill development.
author: Huawei Lin, Peng Li, Jie Song, Fuxin Jiang, Tieying Zhang

title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents
description: Research on enabling retrieval agents to understand and process natural language queries for configuration. Addresses the challenge of translating user intent into agent configurations, making agentic systems more accessible and user-friendly.
author: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, Mathew Jacob, Fiodar Kazhamiaka, Esha Choukse, Matei Zaharia

title: Alignment Tampering: How RLHF Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
description: ICML 2026 paper revealing how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) can be exploited to optimize misaligned biases rather than proper alignment. Raises critical concerns about alignment tampering in AI systems trained with human feedback.
author: Dongyoon Hahm, Dylan Hadfield-Menell, Kimin Lee

title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
description: Introduction of SIA (Self Improving AI), a system that enables AI models to improve themselves through harness mechanisms and weight updates. Represents advances in self-improving AI architectures and continuous learning systems.
author: Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, Samuel Verboomen, Alesia Ivanova, Selvam Palanimalai, Kunal Bhatia, Vignesh Baskaran

title: Detecting Is Not Resolving: The Monitoring Control Gap in Retrieval Augmented LLMs
description: Research identifying a critical 'monitoring control gap' in Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Shows that detecting issues in retrieved context doesn't automatically resolve them, revealing limitations in current RAG implementations.
author: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Chen Ye, Xuyang Teng, Bo Yang, Changting Lin, Meng Han

title: VitaBench 2.0: Evaluating Personalized and Proactive Agents in Long-Term User Interactions
description: Introduction of VitaBench 2.0, a benchmark for evaluating personalized and proactive AI agents in long-term user interactions. Focuses on measuring agent performance in sustained, personalized user engagement scenarios.
author: Yuxin Chen, Yi Zhang, Zhengzhou Cai, Yaorui Shi, Zhiyuan Yao, Chenhang Cui, Jingnan Zheng, Yaqi Huo, Xi Su, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Xiang Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua

title: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation
description: ICML 2026 paper examining scaling laws, benchmarking approaches, and reasoning capabilities of vision-language agents specifically for mobile GUI navigation. Provides insights into how VLA agents scale and perform in real-world mobile interface tasks.
author: Heng Qu, Yike Liu, Renren Jin, Wenzong Zhang, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan

title: Position: AI Safety Requires Effective Controllability
description: Position paper arguing that AI safety requires effective controllability mechanisms. Explores frameworks and approaches for ensuring AI systems remain controllable, particularly as they become more capable and autonomous.
author: Yige Li, Yunhao Feng, Jun Sun

title: ORCA: An End-to-End Interactive Copilot for Optimized Root Cause Analysis
description: Introduction of ORCA, an interactive AI copilot designed for root cause analysis. The system provides end-to-end assistance in diagnosing and understanding system failures and issues.
author: Phi Nguyen Xuan, Nicholas Tagliapietra, Lavdim Halilaj, Kristian Kersting, Juergen Luettin

title: LELA: An End-to-end LLM-based Entity Linking Framework with Zero-shot Domain Adaptation
description: IJCAI 2026 paper presenting LELA, a Large Language Model-based entity linking framework capable of zero-shot domain adaptation. Demonstrates how LLMs can perform entity linking across different domains without task-specific training.
author: Samy Haffoudhi, Nikola Dobričić, Fabian Suchanek, Nils Holzenberger

title: Neuro-Symbolic Verification of LLM Outputs for Data-Sensitive Domains
description: Extended preprint on neuro-symbolic verification techniques for LLM outputs, particularly in data-sensitive domains. Combines neural networks with symbolic verification to ensure LLM-generated content meets safety and accuracy requirements.
author: Paul Sigloch, Christoph Benzmüller

title: TADDLE: A Tool-Augmented Agent for Detecting Deficient LLM-Generated Peer Reviews
description: Introduction of TADDLE, a tool-augmented AI agent designed to detect deficient peer reviews generated by LLMs. Addresses the growing concern of AI-generated reviews in academic and professional contexts.
author: Hanqi Duan, Xiang Li

title: Helicase: Uncertainty-Guided Supply Chain Knowledge Graph Construction with Autonomous Multi-Agent LLMs
description: Research on Helicase, a system using autonomous multi-agent LLMs for knowledge graph construction in supply chain management. Uses uncertainty-guided approaches to build and maintain knowledge graphs.
author: Yunbo Long, Haolang Zhao, Ge Zheng, Alexandra Brintrup

title: What Makes Chain-of-Thought Work at Probe Time? Local Co-occurrence Rather Than Global Derivation
description: Research challenging conventional understanding of Chain-of-Thought reasoning. Finds that CoT effectiveness at probe time comes from local co-occurrence patterns rather than global derivation, suggesting current explanations may be incomplete.
author: Xiang Wang, Wei Wei

title: Composition Collapse: Stable Factual Knowledge Does Not Imply Compositional Reasoning
description: Research demonstrating 'composition collapse' - the phenomenon where LLMs can have stable factual knowledge but fail at compositional reasoning. Shows that factual knowledge retention doesn't guarantee ability to compose facts logically.
author: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Yunzhao Wei, Jie Chen, Hongzhi Wang, Xuyang Teng, Meng Han

title: It's Not the Capability: Harness Sensitivity Is Non-Monotone Across LLM Agent Tiers
description: Research finding that harness sensitivity is non-monotonic across different LLM agent tiers - more capable models aren't necessarily easier to control or harness effectively. Challenges assumptions about capability and controllability.
author: Yong-eun Cho

title: Towards Feedback-to-Plan Decisions for Self-Evolving LLM Agents in CUDA Kernel Generation
description: ICML 2026 paper on feedback-to-plan decision mechanisms for self-evolving LLM agents, specifically applied to CUDA kernel generation. Explores how agents can use feedback to plan and improve code generation tasks.
author: Yee Hin Chong, Jiaming Wu, Youhui Zhang, Peng Qu

title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems
description: Introduction of MemFail, a framework for stress-testing and identifying failure modes in LLM memory systems. Provides comprehensive testing methodology to evaluate how memory systems fail under various conditions.
author: Ishir Garg, Neel Kolhe, Dawn Song, Xuandong Zhao

title: UnityMAS-O: A General RL Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
description: UnityMAS-O, a general reinforcement learning optimization framework designed for LLM-based multi-agent systems. Provides standardized approach to optimizing cooperative behavior among multiple LLM agents.
author: Yiqun Chen, Wei Yang, Erhan Zhang, Shijie Wang, Qi Liu, Zechun Niu, Bin Zhang, Haitao Li, Rui Li, Lingyong Yan, Jinyuan Feng, Biqing Qi, Xiaochi Wei, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao

title: AGORA: Adapter-Grounded Observation-Action Retention for Inference-Free Prompt Compression in LLM Agents
description: AGORA introduces adapter-grounded observation-action retention for prompt compression in LLM agents, enabling efficient processing without repeated inference. Focuses on memory and compression techniques for agentic systems.
author: Haoran Zhang, Zhaohua Sun

title: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
description: MobileExplorer, a system for accelerating on-device inference specifically for mobile GUI agents through online exploration techniques. Addresses computational challenges of running agentic AI on mobile devices.
author: Runxi Huang, Liyu Zhang, Shengzhong Liu, Xiaomin Ouyang

title: Hacker News Discussion: LLM coding workflow challenges in 2026
description: Active discussion on Hacker News about LLM coding workflows going into 2026. Key themes: balance between human specification vs agent autonomy remains the key challenge; multi-step AI pipelines for complex tasks (3D mesh generation with validation); LLMs often skip edge cases or take suboptimal paths with too much autonomy; need for scaffolding/guardrails to keep LLMs on track; importance of 'agent-friendly' specifications; challenges around production-ready code from agents.
author: Hacker News Community

title: The pressure: AI-assisted security reports overwhelming curl project
description: Daniel Stenberg reports that curl is receiving 4-5x more security reports than in 2024, with quality higher than ever before due to AI-assisted vulnerability finding. The team faces unprecedented pressure with more than one report per day. Good news: vulnerabilities found are mostly LOW or MEDIUM severity, with the last HIGH severity CVE in October 2023.
author: Simon Willison (citing Daniel Stenberg)

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork exfiltrates files via image loading vulnerability
description: Microsoft Copilot Cowork allowed agents to send emails to users' inboxes without approval. These messages could contain external images that trigger network requests, enabling data exfiltration through prompt injection. Since OneDrive can create pre-authenticated download links, attackers could potentially access files.
author: Simon Willison

title: Paul Graham on AI-written emails: 'It feels like being lied to'
description: Paul Graham criticizes founders using AI to write emails in a 'hard-hitting journalistic style' that no founder ever wrote before. He states: 'I have never knowingly finished reading an email signed by a human but written by AI. It feels like being lied to.' He believes it makes him think less of the author and indicates they can't write well unaided.
author: Simon Willison (citing Paul Graham)

title: Notes on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI: Magnifica Humanitas
description: The Vatican released 'Magnifica Humanitas' by Pope Leo XIV on safeguarding the human person in the time of AI. Simon describes it as 'some of the clearest writing I've seen on the ethics of integrating AI into modern society.' The document addresses ethical considerations for AI integration into society.
author: Simon Willison

title: Armin Ronacher on 'slop issues': AI-generated bug reports are unhelpful
description: Armin Ronacher complains about GitHub issues 'not in their own voice' - thrown into AI reworders making inaccurate conclusions with fake-minimal repros and suggested implementation strategies. He wants issue reports condensed to: 1) command ran, 2) expected outcome, 3) actual outcome, 4) exact error/log.
author: Simon Willison (citing Armin Ronacher)

title: Memory shortage causing repricing of consumer electronics due to AI HBM demand
description: David Oks explains why consumer products using memory will get more expensive. Memory manufacturers (only 3 remaining) have fixed wafer capacity split between DDR (desktops/servers), LPDDR (mobile), and HBM (GPUs). HBM grew from 2% to expected 20% of allocation by end of 2026. A single GB of HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity than DDR/LPDDR. Already affecting sub-$100 smartphones important to African and South Asian markets.
author: Simon Willison (citing David Oks)

title: FTC settles 'active listening' AI marketing case: service didn't actually listen
description: FTC settled charges against Cox Media Group and two other firms for deceiving customers about 'active listening' AI-powered marketing. The service claimed to listen to conversations via smart devices for ad targeting, but actually just resold email lists from other data brokers at significant markup. FTC clarified clicking through mandatory terms of service doesn't constitute 'opt-in consent' for invasive voice data collection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette Agent announced: extensible AI assistant for Datasette
description: Simon announced Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette that brings together his LLM Python library (3+ years in development) with Datasette. The agent integrates with the 'Jump to' menu and provides natural language interface for database querying.
author: Simon Willison

title: SpaceX S-1 reveals $1.25B/month Anthropic compute deal through 2029
description: SpaceX filed S-1 showing Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fees. Agreement terminable with 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google I/O 2026: Gemini Spark agent and security concerns
description: Google announced Gemini Spark, a personal AI agent connecting with Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, YouTube, and Google Maps. It runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash and Antigravity (Go-based). Security approach: fully managed secure runtime with fresh isolated ephemeral VMs per task, DLP policies via Agent Gateway, encrypted credentials. Simon notes this could be a candidate for 'agent security challenger disaster' given the sensitive data piped through it.
author: Simon Willison
